schema.description: Start an asynchronous task that compresses a site's image assets (jpg/jpeg/png/webp) to webp or avif. Compression REPLACES each asset's hosted file in place — same asset ID, new hostedUrl/contentType/size; the original file is not retained — confirm with the user first. Returns { taskId, status, skippedAssetIds, polling } — poll the task with get_compression_task using the polling hints. Assets already in the target format are skipped; if ALL requested assets are skipped, returns taskId null and status "completed" with no polling hints (no task created). Only one compression task may be pending per site: requesting different work while one is pending returns 409 with the pending taskId in the error message (poll that task and retry after it finishes), while re-requesting the same format and a subset of the pending task's assets returns the pending task's envelope (idempotent retry). Errors: 404 if any requested asset does not exist on the site (or the compression API is not enabled for the environment); 400 if any asset is never-compressible (e.g. svg). Rate limited to 10 requests/min per site.

schema.description: Poll the status of an asset compression task started by compress_assets. Returns { taskId, status } where status is "pending", "completed", or "failed". On completion, also returns result with the target format, counts (assetsQueued/assetsCompressed/assetsSkipped/assetsFailed), total previousByteSize/compressedByteSize, and per-asset outcomes in result.assets — each entry has status ("compressed" | "skipped" | "failed"), a reason on skipped/failed, and the updated hostedUrl/contentType/size on compressed. Failed tasks expose no internal error details; a task pending for more than 15 minutes is reported failed. Poll using the hints from the enqueue response: start at a 1s delay, double up to 10s, and give up after 10 minutes. Returns 404 for an unknown task ID, a task belonging to another site, an expired task (tasks are queryable for ~24h), or when the compression API is not enabled for the environment.

tt.description: Action-type discriminator for how the runtime executes this action on trigger. Optional — omitting it is usually the safest default: the host infers it from the properties value shapes you sent (a [from, to] pair → 2; a [from]-only value → 1; a bare scalar or [null, to] infers nothing and is read as 0). Set it explicitly only when the shapes can't express what you mean — most often 3 for a Set. Enum (source: TweenType in the IX3 runtime): 0=To (animate current value → the given target — the common case, e.g. a click-triggered fade or move into a resting state), 1=From (jump to the given value, then animate back to the element's native/current value — reveal-style presets like preset-drop-in/preset-pop-in), 2=FromTo (explicit start AND end, e.g. preset-slide-in-left/preset-scale-in), 3=Set (instant, non-tweened assignment, no duration — e.g. setting display:none after a fade completes). presetId.description:
Which built-in IX3 preset this action was authored from — optional, with no runtime effect (it's only copied into the action's GSAP tween metadata; tt above is what the runtime actually branches on). Its table is a convenient starting point for picking a tt/properties combination:

  preset-fade-out        tt=0  wf:transform.opacity: [null,'0%']
  preset-slide-in-left   tt=2  opacity:['0%','100%'], xPercent:[-100,0]
  preset-slide-out-right tt=0  opacity:[null,'0%'], xPercent:[null,100]
  preset-slide-in-up     tt=1  opacity:['0%',null], yPercent:[100,null]
  preset-slide-out-down  tt=0  opacity:[null,'0%'], yPercent:[null,100]
  preset-scale-in        tt=2  scale:[0,1]
  preset-pop-in          tt=1  scale:[0,null]
  preset-drop-in         tt=1  y:[-300,null], opacity:['0%',null]  — prefer a yPercent preset instead of raw pixel y (see properties field)
  preset-set-action      tt=3  instant/non-tweened, e.g. {display:'none'}
A To action animates from whatever value the element already has, so the reveal shapes that carry a start value are tt=2 with opacity:['0%','100%'] and tt=1 with opacity:['0%',null] (action guide, Resting state).
There is no preset-grow/preset-shrink. Staggered variants are preset-staggered-fade-in (tt=1), -fade-out (tt=0), -fade-drop-in (tt=1), -fade-fall-out (tt=0), all with stagger:{each:0.05}. staggered-fade-in is tt=1 where fade-in is tt=0, so it carries a start value. Use it to turn a role name like "Contractor" into the site_role_id a write needs, or to resolve a roles.siteRoleId read off a member to its name. Match custom roles on name and built-ins on siteRole — a custom role can be named "Marketer". Not paginated.

workspace_id.description: Workspace id. Discover it with data_workspaces_tool > list_workspaces.

email.description: Return only the member and invite matching this exact email address. Omit to list everyone.

roles.description: Return only members holding one of these workspace roles, as a comma-separated list — e.g. "admin,member". Accepts owner, admin, member, guest, reviewer, public, client; a value outside that set is rejected. Wider than the set that can be granted (owner, public and client cannot be assigned, but can be filtered on).

limit.description: Rows per page, 1-100, applied to members and invites separately — so a page can carry up to twice this many rows. Values above 100 are rejected.

cursor.description: pagination.nextCursor from a previous response, to fetch the following page. It is opaque and covers both lists at once, and it is bound to the filters it was issued under: changing email or roles invalidates it, and a changed query starts without one. Stop when it comes back null.

schema.description: List a workspace's members and its invites. Returns two separate lists: members, each with id, email, firstName, lastName, roles (roles.workspace, plus roles.site where one is set), and addedOn (a timestamp, or null for a legacy row with none recorded) — addedOn is the MOST RECENT join, not member-since: it resets on a remove-and-re-add but not on a role change, and for an invite it is acceptance time, not send time. Invites, each with id, email, role, createdOn and a status of pending, declined or expired — so the invite list is not only outstanding ones. Pass email to resolve one person to a member id, the lookup step before a site grant when you only have an address. Both lists share one cursor; pagination.nextCursor is null once exhausted and always present, so null is the end signal rather than absence. Filters match on exact email and on roles; there is no search by display name.

workspace_id.description: Workspace id. Discover it with data_workspaces_tool > list_workspaces.

schema.description: Set one workspace role on many members and pending invites at once — the alternative to repeating update_workspace_role per person. Seat checks apply to the whole batch: if it would exceed available seats it is rejected outright and nothing is applied.

schema.description: Invite someone to a workspace by email. For admin, member, and reviewer invites, initial site access must be named exactly one of two ways: default_site_role for the same role on every workspace site, or site_access for the same role on specific sites only (an invite stores one site role, so per-site roles are not possible until the invitee accepts) — providing both, or neither, is rejected. A client invite creates collaborator client access and requires exactly one site_access entry; default_site_role is not accepted. The response is one of two shapes, told apart by its status field. status 'invited' means an invite was created and the person has NO access until they accept and sign up — details are under invite. status 'active' means the address already belonged to a workspace member and nothing was created — details are under member, including their existing addedOn (see list_workspace_members for what it means). Reporting both as added would tell the user someone has access when they have only been asked. Consumes a seat and fails when none are available.

schema.description: Change one existing workspace member's role. Use bulk_update_workspace_roles for several people at once. schema.description: Partially update a site's AEO recommendation settings. Provide at least one of ruleConfig or recurringAuditsEnabled. Omitted fields stay unchanged. Returns the fully resolved settings document. Requires sites:write. This writes to the live site configuration.
